purpose: Compare oracle and event-data source models before lending, liquidation, perps, stable-value, bridge, or prediction claims are upgraded.

sourceReferences.name: Kaskad oracle article
sourceReferences.notes: Kaskad describes an internal V1 off-chain oracle and liquidation engine, weighted median price feeds, exchange reliability weighting, and a later move toward an on-chain Kaspa L2 model.

sourceReferences.name: Eliott Mea oracle interview
sourceReferences.notes: Frames the oracle problem around CEX order-book falsifiability, median-oracle information loss, no-arbitrage ground truth, and why oracle dishonesty is not objectively slashable like invalid consensus behavior.

sourceReferences.name: Kaskad roadmap
sourceReferences.notes: Tracks Kaskad's phased lending, oracle, cross-chain, L2, and eventual L1/covenant or vProg direction.

sourceReferences.name: Kaskad architecture
sourceReferences.notes: Useful for separating Igra/EVM lending architecture from this repo's TN12 L1 covenant and payload/indexer model.

sourceReferences.name: Kaskad lending mechanics
sourceReferences.notes: Useful for supply, borrow, health factor, risk parameter, and liquidation terminology.

models.name: CEX weighted median feed
models.possibleUse: Display prices, risk warnings, off-chain simulations, lending dashboard research
models.manipulationModel: A source venue can publish false, frozen, or non-actionable quotes; a median can hide outliers but also lag or discard real market moves.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Flag stale venues, discount unreliable venues, pause custody-moving actions, and require human or governance review before liquidation claims.
models.determinism: Not deterministic from Kaspa consensus; depends on off-chain observation and reporter policy.
models.repoUseNow: Can inform a simulation-only oracle risk dashboard.

models.name: Arbitrage-simulated fair price
models.dataSource: Cross-venue order books plus modeled executable arbitrage paths
models.possibleUse: Research target for fair-value computation and anomaly detection
models.manipulationModel: The model can still inherit false venue data, latency, missing liquidity, fee assumptions, and non-executable routes.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Record model inputs, venues, fees, timestamps, and actionable-route assumptions; use for review prompts before settlement.
models.determinism: Model-deterministic only if all inputs and route rules are fixed and archived.
models.repoUseNow: Can become an archived oracle-update payload format, not an enforcement source.

models.name: Signed reporter attestation set
models.dataSource: Named reporters, watchers, pools, or services signing observations
models.possibleUse: Accepted payload event stream, review prompts, prediction or hedge simulator inputs
models.manipulationModel: Reporters can collude, go stale, copy the same upstream source, or sign self-serving observations.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Track signer provenance, quorum, recency, conflicts, reputation, and review-only status until penalties or challenge rules exist.
models.determinism: Deterministic only for signature validity and accepted payload inclusion, not factual truth.
models.repoUseNow: Matches current attestation registry and prediction/hedge simulator boundaries.

models.name: Miner or RTD sampling
models.dataSource: Miner, pool, or low-latency watcher observations
models.possibleUse: Fast awareness, latency research, review prompts, pool-policy signals
models.manipulationModel: Signals can be spammed, bribed, selectively withheld, centralized by pool share, or mistaken for objective block-header facts.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Require signed reports, pool identity, conflict sets, anti-spam thresholds, and review-only routing before any custody impact.
models.determinism: Accepted payload inclusion is deterministic; the observed external event is not.
models.repoUseNow: Can extend the miner-signal research fixture and attestation registry.

models.name: On-chain DCLOB or native market source
models.dataSource: A liquid, on-chain order book or native market with executable quotes
models.possibleUse: Long-term price source for lending and liquidation if liquidity is deep enough
models.manipulationModel: Market manipulation remains possible, but quote falsification is reduced when orders are executable and settled on-chain.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Use executable order state, liquidity depth, batch or ordering rules, and circuit breakers.
models.determinism: Potentially deterministic once execution, ordering, liquidity, and settlement rails exist.
models.repoUseNow: Do not build against this yet; use as a target dependency for DEX/AMM and lending briefs.

models.name: Source-chain or bridge anchor
models.dataSource: External-chain headers, finality proofs, bridge reporter quorum, or ZK proof public inputs
models.possibleUse: Bridge, wrapped-asset, source-chain settlement, cross-chain app proofs
models.manipulationModel: A proof may verify computation without proving canonical source-chain truth, custody solvency, or safe exits.
models.staleOrWrongHandling: Name the anchored object, finality rule, challenge path, custody holder, outage behavior, and user exit rule.
models.determinism: Deterministic only for the proof/check being verified, not for every trust assumption around the bridge.
models.repoUseNow: Can become a bridge-anchor brief only after the anchored object is explicit.

claimRules: Use oracle sources for display or review before using them for custody, liquidation, settlement, or automated payout.
Accepted Kaspa payload inclusion proves the report was recorded, not that the report is true.
Median or weighted feeds reduce some source risk but do not create deterministic ground truth.
Kaskad's work is a research and architecture reference here; do not imply this TN12 repo has Kaskad lending or oracle infrastructure.
A lending, perps, bridge, or stable-value app needs an explicit stale/wrong-data response before it can become user-facing.
boundaries: This matrix is an oracle research artifact, not a live oracle integration.
It can justify review prompts, simulations, and app briefs, not automated liquidation or settlement.
Kaskad and Eliott Mea sources are treated as research leads until their assumptions are remapped to this repo's payload, indexer, wallet, and TN12 covenant rails.
No model here is custody-ready without stale-feed, challenge, signer, and settlement rules.
